az_fay_buttress.blurb: Fay Buttress is a tall sandstone wall tucked at the head of Fay Canyon, in the Dry Creek country west of Sedona. It holds ten climbs, nearly all of them trad, with a single top-rope line. Most routes are long multi-pitch outings of four to five pitches, and the grades start at 5.10 and climb to 5.13, with the bulk of them in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. This is a place for experienced parties comfortable with traditional protection and a long day, not a beginner crag. Reaching the base means a hike up the canyon wash and a steep, loose path to the wall, so budget real time before you start climbing.

az_hub.blurb: HUB is a small bouldering cluster on the hillside of Panther Peak, in the Tucson Mountains west of the city. The centerpiece is a broad flat block perched on another, which creates a roof that wraps around it, and several steeper lines sit on the uphill face. There are ten problems, ranging from V0 to V4, with most of them at V2. The stone is rough volcanic conglomerate studded with cobbles, so expect pebbly holds and rock that can vary in quality. A fair uphill hike through desert brush is needed to get here, so it suits a half-day session more than a quick stop.

az_bat_roof_the.blurb: The Bat Roof is a pocketed roof sector within Priest Draw, a bouldering zone south of Flagstaff that is climbed on limestone. It is mostly a boulder spot with ten lines: a cluster of easier problems from V1 to V3, a few harder ones in the V4 to V7 range, and a single roped sport line. The roof problems are steep and rely on pockets, a style that often feels unfamiliar but suits climbers used to gym-style steep climbing. The area can generally be reached across most of the year, making it a handy option when other Flagstaff crags are out of season.

az_memorial_wall.blurb: Memorial Wall is a short cliff in Christopher Creek Gorge, in the Tonto National Forest east of Payson. It carries ten routes, seven sport and three trad, with grades from about 5.6 up to 5.11, and a good number of mid-range lines around 5.9. The wall sits up a climbers' path above the creek, behind thick brush, and many routes are named in honor of military service. The gorge is a good cool-season destination, but midsummer is hot and buggy, so plan for spring, fall or winter.

_expect.name: Great Leaders of the World Wall

az_great_leaders_of_the_world_wall.blurb: Great Leaders of the World Wall is a one-pitch cliff in the Superstition Mountains, on the Weaver's Needle side of the trail east of Phoenix. All ten climbs are trad, running from easy 5.5 and 5.6 lines through a core of 5.9 and 5.10 routes up to one 5.12. Expect a long hike from the Peralta trailhead, roughly an hour over Fremont Saddle toward Pinon Camp. The wall tends to be sunny, and the range's volcanic rock can be loose in spots, so test holds as you go. This is a quiet backcountry destination for self-reliant parties rather than a roadside crag.
